data.gender_notes: Cassandre is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Cassandra was a Trojan princess who was granted the gift of prophecy by Apollo but was cursed that no one would believe her. Derived from Greek kassandra, meaning 'helenize' or 'emasculate'. The name Cassandre carries the meaning “Ancient Greek prophetess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Cassandre usually hope their child will grow to embody ancient greek prophetess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine prophecy and unheeded warnings.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cassandre total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Cassandra's story is a warning against the arrogance of ignoring the warnings of those with knowledge or ability to foresee the future. This name is a reminder of the importance of listening and taking action based on the advice of others, even if that advice is unpalatable or goes against popular opinion.
data.spiritual_significance: Cassandra's story also serves as a reminder of the power of God's prophecy and the importance of remaining open to His messages, even when confronted with skepticism or disbelief. The name Cassandra encourages us to trust in the wisdom and guidance of the Divine, and to remain steadfast in our faith, even when faced with adversity or rejected by those around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Cassandre is derived from the Greek seer Cassandra, who was blessed with the gift of prophecy but cursed to be never believed. In Christianity, Cassandre may symbolize the struggle to share God's truth with a skeptical world, or the challenge of bearing heavy burdens of knowledge and responsibility with faith.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Cassandra was a Trojan princess, daughter of King Priam and Hecuba. The name Cassandre carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
In Greek mythology, Cassandra was granted the gift of prophecy by Apollo, but she was cursed that no one would believe her prophecies.
